summary: Replace micromark-extension-directive's flow-level container construct (whose nested content is re-tokenized once per enclosing level) with a legion-owned micromark document construct in packages/proof-editor, so nested content is tokenized once; bound directive nesting at 32 in the browser (an opener past 32 open blocks reads as text, refused in the default mode) and in Go (a typed block inside 32 typed blocks is refused on write); keep the 84 committed pmdoc fixtures byte-identical except frontmatter-opener-unclosed, which changes together with a Go frontmatterAttempt wrap of typedDirectiveParser.

implement: legion-worker: the proof on a production-like surface (Conversation tab in Chromium against the real Go server and Postgres), the PR body template, the push and handoff rules, and the production check after the close (references/pr-body.md, references/merge-gate.md)
ce-simplify-code: the one simplify pass the implementer runs in its first round, since the diff touches runtime code
dispatch: the production check's record on the issue (the deployment's Dispatch production check output) is a Dispatch write
test: legion-worker: re-run the implementer's e2e command on the tester's own lane, add the tester's own proof and negative control, and try to break the bound (references/pr-body.md)
review: legion-worker: review the head by SHA, the merge gate and the PR body's Look at first / Not proven lines (references/merge-gate.md, references/review-threads.md)

trickyParts: micromark-extension-directive's package exports only `.`; its factory helpers must be copied, never deep-imported (Vite and Node refuse the path).
micromark's checkNewContainers runs a container start inside effects.check and throws its events away, so a depth counter must not count a start that only ran in a check.
micromark copies its token stack in every attempt (create-tokenizer.js:476): each line costs O(depth^2) with a document construct, which is why the bound is needed.

As a document construct, the rest of the opener's line and of the closing fence's line reaches flow as a blank line (lineEndingBlank) and changes list spread; the old construct consumed it as lineEnding.
A `:::` line closes the outermost open block whose fence it satisfies, and everything inside it, in both parsers; 32 nested closed typed blocks need fences that shorten inwards.
micromark must stay 4.0.2 in bun.lock: 4.0.3 makes quotes, nested lists and setext headings quadratic (micromark/micromark#246).

The e2e harness is not in the image: Postgres 17 with pgvector and Playwright's Chromium are built on the issue volume (docs/solutions/testing/a-browser-harness-in-an-issue-pod-lives-on-the-issue-volume-INFRA-43.md), on the lane's own five ports and database (LEGION-695's solution doc).
Do not post either input to production: a reader whose tab still runs the old build freezes.

findings.finding: The parity gate contradicted itself: 'fixtures unchanged' and 'JS matches Go' are the same requirement because TestParseMatchesMilkdownForFixtures holds Go to every fixture, and frontmatter-opener-unclosed cannot be kept without a Go change since a micromark document construct opens nothing after an unclosed front-matter opener.
findings.answer: Design section 3: every fixture byte-identical except frontmatter-opener-unclosed, which changes only together with a Go frontmatterAttempt wrap of typedDirectiveParser; any other fixture the browser cannot reproduce goes to the architect before a Go reading changes.

findings.finding: A bound of 100 leaves input 1 near or over 1 s (1.07 s cold in the spike) and a 2.5-4.5 s cost on 100-deep bodies Go accepts.
findings.answer: Bound chosen at 32 in both parsers, with a Go write refusal; measured 0.29-0.31 s for input 1 and at most 1.6x the no-directive cost for 32,000-char worst cases.

findings.finding: The JS bound counts only directives while Go's 100 counts every container; nested list items followed by blank lines may still be slow.
findings.answer: Measured: 100 nested list items then blank lines take 7.5 s at main, a micromark core cost with no `:::` in it. The plan keeps the directive-only bound (Go gets a typed-block-only bound of 32, the same count) and reports the list case to the architect as part of the spec departure on the general sub-second claim.

findings.finding: Dropping the spec's general sub-second requirement needs the owner's decision, and its evidence was bun-only.
findings.answer: Recorded as a spec departure with Node/V8 and Go numbers added (micromark alone 0.8 s for 8,000 list items in Node 24; Go 0.5 s); named in the completion summary for the architect.

findings.finding: What is timed was ambiguous; an absolute wall-clock bound goes against repo practice; MarkdownPreview with fullTitle parses twice.
findings.answer: A1 is measured as the largest main-thread gap from navigation until the card draws, by an in-page heartbeat that works in both e2e projects; the Go test uses cpuTimeOf with a wide margin (ms vs 1 s); the proof-editor regression lock uses a 5 s bound against ~0.3 s; the Conversation tab is the spec's surface and the bound makes every surface's parse cheap.

findings.finding: A1's negative control and the production check were missing; 66.3 s was measured before #2303.

findings.answer: Stated out of scope in the plan's last section: they get the same bound, so their nesting cost is linear; their baseline parse cost is not this issue's.

findings.finding: The default engine would silently read a 33rd typed opener as text while Go refuses it; the 32-deep test must state its fences.
findings.answer: Design section 2: the default mode throws a refusal naming the line; task 1 states the fences (shortening inwards, or unclosed); AGENTS.md records the extra allowed edit if the refusal lands in block-schema.ts.

findings.finding: The Go test proves nothing new (it passes at base) and its entry point was unnamed.
findings.answer: ParseForWrite named (the API's document write path, docs/tree.go:104-132); it is A1's Go test as the spec asks; the red Go test is the new 32/33 typed-block bound.

findings.finding: 'Mirroring Go's Open/Continue model' was imprecise: Go opens only :::name{...}.
findings.answer: Design section 1 says the JS grammar stays as it is; only the container structure (closing fence checked from the outermost block inwards) matches Go.

findings.finding: Several claims (timings, the micromark 4.0.3 regression, spec approval) were unverified by the analyst.
findings.answer: Timings are the planner's own runs on this pod, recorded with their inputs in measurements; the micromark regression is linked (micromark/micromark#246, read 2026-10-27); the child spec needs no approval of its own under the root's design gate.

specDepartures.spec: Change 2: make each parse of a text no larger than the body cap finish in well under a second in all three engines.
specDepartures.plan: Bounds the cost `:::` nesting adds (at most about 1.6x the same body without it, at the bound of 32) and gets both of the spec's inputs to about 0.3 s; does not make every 32,000-character body parse well under a second.
specDepartures.evidence: At main with no `:::`: 8,000 list items (32,000 chars) take 1.6-1.7 s in the headless engine and 0.8 s in micromark alone under Node 24; Go ParseForWrite 0.50 s; 100 nested list items followed by blank lines 7.5 s headless (micromark checks every open list item on each blank line).

summary: The general sub-second parse of any text under the body cap is not delivered; the plan delivers sub-second drawing of the spec's two inputs and a bounded, linear cost for `:::` nesting.
outcome.scope: Plain-markdown baseline cost and nested-list-with-blank-lines cost are outside this plan; the architect decides whether they belong to this issue.

specDepartures.spec: Change 2 offers a parse fix, or a refusal on write of nesting deeper than a limit together with drawing an already-stored body that exceeds it as plain text.
specDepartures.plan: Both together: a parse fix (a legion-owned micromark document construct) and a limit of 32 nested blocks; Go refuses a document past it on write, and a stored comment past it is not drawn whole as plain text: only the openers past the limit read as text lines and the rest of the body keeps its formatting.
specDepartures.evidence: A limit alone leaves 7.8 s at depth 25 for a 32,000-char body; the construct alone leaves input 1 at 36.7 s (micromark's per-attempt token-stack copy); together, 0.3 s.

specDepartures.spec: The spec names no change to how the server reads a document.
specDepartures.plan: Go also reads a typed block that follows an unclosed front-matter opener the way the new browser construct does (frontmatterAttempt around typedDirectiveParser), and refuses a typed block nested inside 32 typed blocks on write.
specDepartures.evidence: A micromark document construct opens nothing while micromark tries front matter from a leading `---` to the end (pmdoc/lines.go:120-127), and TestParseMatchesMilkdownForFixtures (pmdoc/parse_test.go:12-28) holds Go to the browser's reading of every fixture.

outcome.scope: Adds two Go reading changes for documents: the front-matter rule for typed blocks, and the 32-typed-block write bound (packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md and CHANGELOG updated).
